issue.title: December 2026 usage limits: preserve access to ChatGPT High and Codex/Work on Plus

labels.name: rate-limits
labels.description: Issues related to rate limits, quotas, and token usage reporting

issue.body:
## Executive summary

Thank you to the OpenAI team for continuing to make your most capable models and powerful AI experiences accessible to Plus subscribers. I am genuinely grateful for the opportunities this has given me as an individual creator.

**Please preserve the ability to use ChatGPT High and Codex/Work together on Plus without losing access to advanced reasoning after a long agent session. I would welcome a shared allowance if it preserves or improves the practical capacity available today.**

I want to remain a paying customer and eventually upgrade to Pro. **If the December change materially reduces the value of Plus, I will have to reconsider renewing my subscription and upgrading, and seriously evaluate competing AI services.**

Before the December transition, I respectfully ask OpenAI to:

1. **Protect advanced reasoning from exhaustion by Codex/Work.**
   - **Preferred:** Retain separate allowances.
   - **Acceptable alternative:** A shared allowance that demonstrably preserves or improves existing mixed workflows.
   - **Minimum safeguard if a shared pool cannot achieve this:** Reserve advanced reasoning capacity that agent work cannot consume, even if it uses capable earlier-generation models.
2. **Publish concrete before/after usage examples.** Explain included capacity, model-specific consumption, reset rules, and what remains available after a limit is reached.
3. **Evaluate the effect on customer growth.** Consider completed workflows, retention, and voluntary upgrades alongside compute costs.

*Updated November 25, 2026. Originally opened October 31, 2026; the announced policy was noted on November 9.*

## 1. The problem: reasoning and execution are one workflow

OpenAI's [usage-limit guidance](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001625-understanding-chatgpt-and-codex-usage-limits) announces a shared ChatGPT and Codex allowance for Plus, Pro, and Business beginning in December. It describes token-based accounting, with Instant chat excluded, and states that most users are not expected to wait for resets more frequently.

I appreciate that objective. My concern is whether it will hold for subscribers who rely heavily on both products.

I use **ChatGPT High to research, design, and make decisions**, and **Codex/Work to implement, test, and verify**. Consider a typical mixed workflow:

- Plan a feature and its requirements using advanced reasoning.
- Run a sustained implementation and testing session.
- Return to advanced reasoning to assess the results, resolve trade-offs, and decide what to do next.

If the implementation stage exhausts the shared allowance, the final stage may become unavailable. Instant chat is useful, but it is not an equivalent substitute for advanced reasoning on complex decisions.

Please compare how much of this **think → build → verify** workflow subscribers can complete before and after the transition, including cases where one workload is particularly demanding. I would rather see representative end-to-end examples than an overall average alone.

## 2. My own journey: OpenAI's upgrade strategy was already working

I began as a Free user. ChatGPT was genuinely useful even without a subscription. I wanted more image generation and more consistent access to higher-quality conversations. When Go became available at a price I could afford, I subscribed.

Later, I wanted an AI agent that could help me build software and create a social platform. When I discovered that Codex was available on Plus, upgrading felt absolutely worth it. Projects I had previously only imagined became possible to pursue.

**Free → Go → Plus → Pro (my next goal).**

I am not a funded startup or an established business. I am an individual creator building projects and a multi-role AI team, working toward my first business income. I hope to upgrade to Pro when my work and finances justify it, and to use paid APIs and other services as my projects grow.

When Sam Altman described the [“revenge of the idea guys” at Stripe Sessions 2026](https://stripe.com/sessions/2026/a-conversation-with-sam-altman), he spoke positively about AI opening new opportunities for founders who understand their users even if they cannot code. That resonated deeply with me. My journey from Free to Go to Plus, and my ambition to build a business and eventually upgrade to Pro, reflect the very opportunity he was describing. I want to turn that possibility into something real with OpenAI.

**OpenAI made me want to pay more by expanding what I could accomplish, not by making my existing experience worse.**

I recognize that advanced inference and long-running agents have real costs. I do not have access to OpenAI's internal economics, but my own experience illustrates why affordable entry points and compelling upgrades matter. It also aligns with CFO Sarah Friar's [discussion of how personal adoption supports workplace and developer adoption](https://openai.com/index/the-work-now-within-reach/).

Greater agent capacity, concurrency, and sophisticated AI team capabilities would give me meaningful reasons to upgrade voluntarily. Preserving the practical value of Plus while I work toward my first income would help keep that path to Pro open.

Predictable subscription costs matter to individual creators. If additional capacity needs to be sold separately, an optional, transparently priced fixed-capacity add-on would be preferable to unpredictable credit purchases. This is not a request for a mandatory price increase.

## 3. Dots on Plus: a related opportunity

I welcome the expansion of dots to Plus. A dependable personal assistant for conversation, routine scheduled tasks, and ongoing project coordination could make the transition more valuable.

I am not asking for Pro-equivalent entitlements or unlimited autonomous computation on Plus. Compute-intensive work can reasonably have separate budgets, while Pro can offer greater capacity and concurrency.

Please clarify the Plus allowances for conversation and autonomous work, how routine tasks and delegated Work/Codex execution are counted, and what remains available when a limit is reached. My hope is that everyday assistance remains dependable even when heavier work reaches its budget.

This is a complementary opportunity, not a prerequisite for my primary request.

## Why I hope to keep growing with OpenAI

I took seriously the vision described by Sam Altman and Jakub Pachocki in [*Built to benefit everyone: our plan*](https://openai.com/index/built-to-benefit-everyone-our-plan/): making personal AGI accessible to everyone. I do not interpret that vision as a promise of unlimited free compute, but as a reason to believe that individuals can start building before they have the resources of an established business.

**Please keep the path from a first idea to a first product, a first income, and eventually a business that can pay OpenAI more open.**

I want to stay with OpenAI, recommend its products, and grow with them. If the December transition genuinely improves our ability to think, create, and build, I will sincerely welcome it.

Thank you for considering this feedback from a paying Plus customer.

Related usability request: [#41361](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41361) — allow informed users to opt out of the five-hour Codex cap without increasing their weekly allowance.

---

### Related independent community petitions

Other subscribers commenting on this issue have also shared these **independently organized Change.org petitions** asking OpenAI to keep advanced ChatGPT reasoning and Codex allowances separate:

- [Keep ChatGPT High Reasoning and Codex Quotas Separate — December 2026](https://www.change.org/p/keep-chatgpt-high-reasoning-and-codex-quotas-separate-december-2026) — shared in [this comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/58530#issuecomment-6571936904).
- [OpenAI: Keep ChatGPT and Codex Usage Limits Separate!](https://www.change.org/KeepChatGPTAndCodexSeparate) — shared in [this comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/58530#issuecomment-6574426802).

These petitions are **community initiatives, not official OpenAI campaigns**. I am linking them so reviewers can see related concerns and additional subscriber perspectives.

comment.body:
I support this request as a paying ChatGPT Pro subscriber. I use ChatGPT's advanced reasoning for research, learning, and planning software projects, while Codex is essential for implementing and testing them. These are distinct, complementary workflows. Sharing one allowance would force users to choose between thinking deeply and coding.

My Codex weekly allowance was exhausted in a week when my Profile showed roughly 1.1B tokens of activity. I understand that this total isn't necessarily the actual quota, which makes clear, model-weighted usage accounting and a transparent before/after comparison all the more important.

Please keep ChatGPT High reasoning and Codex allowances independent. At minimum, provide a guaranteed High-reasoning reserve Codex cannot exhaust, explain exactly how shared usage will be counted, and avoid reducing practical access for existing Pro subscribers at the same price.
